question.text: The dissociation constant of acetic is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mo> </mo><mo>×</mo><mo> </mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>–</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo></math>. When <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>25</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mL</mi><mo> </mo><mi>of</mi><mo> </mo><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">M</mi><mo> </mo><msub><mi>CH</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mi>COONa</mi></math> solution is mixed with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>25</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mL</mi><mo> </mo><mi>of</mi><mo> </mo><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>02</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">M</mi><mo> </mo><msub><mi>CH</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mi>COOH</mi></math> solution, the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>pH</mi></math> of the resultant solution is found to be equal to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi></math> is _______.

solution.text:
The Henderson equation for the given acidic buffer can be written as 

pH=pKa+logsaltweak acid

5=pKa+log25×0.225×0.02⇒pKa=4⇒Ka=10-4=10×10-5

Hence, the value of x is 10.
